newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher, trading remains subdued.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher, trading remains subdued.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed moderately higher on Friday after drifting in a narrow range for most of the day, sandwiched by a national holiday on Thursday and the weekend. Brokers expected the top to be capped next week, as the market lacked factors to stimulate fresh buying.
The key 225-share Nikkei average rose 97.33 points or 0.47 percent to close at 20,968.16. Its December futures gained 130 points to 21,040.
"Since there are no specific factors to inspire buying, the Nikkei is likely to be trapped between 20,500 and 21,500 next week," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities.
The share price of the consumer electronics parts maker was up 80 yen to close at 1,130 yen.

Green Cross Corp fell on news on Wednesday that three former presidents of the drug firm had been indicted on charges of professional negligence resulting in the death of a patient from the company's sale of HIV-tainted products in the 1980s. The share was down 20 yen at 392 yen.
The second section index dropped 10.63 points to 2,054.71, with 7.6 million shares traded, while the over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 5.99 points to end at 1,532.78.
